sections.heading: C — Vehicle Control and Speed
sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle Control and Speed

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
No book alone builds a safe driver; crash risk shrinks with experience earned through lessons and practice [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Start the car by its owner manual, since steps differ with fuel injection and transmission type [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Automatics shift themselves while you pick Park to lock, Reverse to back, Neutral to idle, and Drive to go [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Low caps engine speed and may appear as gears 3, 2, and 1 marking the top gear allowed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A02
Manual gears gate speed ranges, climbing Neutral and 1 through 2, 3, 4, and beyond via the clutch third pedal [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A02
Shift manuals in three beats: clutch down with the left foot, lever moved with the right hand, then gas eased as the clutch releases [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A02
Repeat the clutch dance to downshift, to halt, and to back up from Neutral or 1 into Reverse [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
Feed speed smoothly, since jackrabbit starts spin wheels and skid, especially on slick roads, and manuals demand clutch-gas balance against racing or stalling [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
Stopping hinges on car weight, size, load, and tires plus your foot-to-brake reaction, and smooth halts take practice [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
Gravel, snow, ice, and even dry asphalt skid under harsh braking, and speed stretches every stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
Stopping distance sums reaction and braking spans: 69 feet at 20 mph, 123 feet at 30 mph, and 189 feet at 40 mph [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
Higher speeds compound the sum: 268 feet at 50 mph, 359 feet at 60 mph, and 464 feet at 70 mph [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A03
Hold a 3- to 4-second gap ahead where collisions lurk most, a rule valid only in normal traffic and fair weather [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A03
Beginners keep at least three seconds normally, while veterans may trim to two seconds in kind conditions [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A03
Past 40 mph stretch to four or five seconds, and on slick roads or behind view-blocking vehicles stretch to six or more [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A03
With ABS, stomp and hold the pedal through its pushback without releasing, after studying the owner manual [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A03
Warn of surprise slows or tailgaters with three or four quick brake taps [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A03
Always halt at stop signs, flashing reds before proceeding if clear, and red lights even where right on red is legal [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A03
Also halt before sidewalks leaving private roads, entering public roads from drives and lots, for officers, and for work-zone flaggers [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A03
Halt for blind pedestrians with white or red-tipped canes or guide dogs whenever they near your path [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A03
Time gaps by landmark: your bumper must not reach the marker before your slow count of three [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A04
Posted limits cap legal speed for ideal roads, so temper pace to signs, surface, and sky; 60 mph needs triple the stopping room of 30 mph [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A04
Unposted caps run 20 mph in business zones, 25 mph in residential and school zones, and 45 mph in suburbs and for towing rigs [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A04
Further unposted caps run 50 mph on dark unsurfaced secondaries and for trucks on secondaries anytime, 60 mph on primaries, urban interstates, and daylit secondaries, and 70 mph on rural interstates, with lower postings possible [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A04
Crawling crashes too, so match traffic flow, and shun interstates below their 40 mph minimum [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A04
Grip opposite wheel sides at 9 and 3 or lower at 7 and 5 to tame airbags and keep command [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A04
Scan far ahead to pre-plan steering, and corner with hand-over-hand or push-pull [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A04
Shun one-palm turns that surrender control, and unwind the wheel by hand rather than letting it slither free [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0042]

Misconceptions: posted limits are maximums for ideal roads, not everyday targets; ABS wants a hard held pedal rather than pumping; slow driving can crash as surely as speeding.

Mnemonic: gap three, rain six; business twenty, homes twenty-five, rural interstate seventy; pump never the ABS.

Glossary: stopping distance (reaction plus braking distance); ABS (antilock brakes that stop without skidding); hand-over-hand (a cornering wheel technique); low gear (a capped gear range for engine braking).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every control and speed rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
